newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P assigns A/A-1 ratings to TransAlta NZ.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns A/A-1 ratings to TransAlta NZ.

text.p: Standard and Poor's on Wednesday said it had assigned its 'A' long term and 'A-1' short term ratings to TransAlta New Zealand Ltd, to be formed from the proposed merger of Energy Direct Corp and unlisted Wellington utility Capital Power.

"The preliminary ratings reflect TransAlta NZ's expected solid financial profile and outlook, its stable business environment, and strong operational performance, stemming from the merging entities," S&P said in a statement.
The rating outlook would be stable.
After the amalgamation, TransAlta NZ would be New Zealand's fourth largest electricity supply company, S&P said.

"TransAlta NZ's operational performance is likely to be very good. The company will benefit from synergies both between the existing electricity business of Energy Direct and Capital Power, and with the gas business of Energy Direct," S&P said.
The agency said TransAlta NZ's stable business position stemmed from a predictable revenue stream from its electricity wires and gas pipes network which provide the bulk of earnings.
Shareholders of EnergyDirect and Capital Power will vote on the merger proposal next Monday and it will take effect on October 1 if approved. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
